commands.description: Bound new feature or epic work by resolving missing material constraints before drafting planning artifacts.
commands.execution_context: Use when scope, success criteria, or constraints remain unclear. Reuse supplied answers and source evidence; ask only questions whose missing answers would change the plan, through the available harness question primitive.

argument_schema.name: request
argument_schema.description: Optional feature or epic ask, including any already supplied constraints and acceptance criteria.

loop: inspect the request and existing evidence; identify only missing material constraints
ask targeted questions where needed, without a fixed question count or repeating supplied answers
record answers, assumptions, scope boundaries, and success criteria as durable decisions; if MCP is unavailable, emit them in the worker report for coordinator recording
bound MVP scope and exclusions, then hand off to assessment or spec drafting
model downstream work as a dependency DAG; require real behavior RED evidence before dependent implementation while admitting independent groups concurrently

commands.makefile_target: (in-session advisory skill; no standalone make target)
commands.description: Structured refactoring evaluation: identify design smells, sequence behavior-preserving remediations.
commands.execution_context: Use when evaluating code health, smell audits, or tech-debt assessment for a module, package, or workflow — not for branch review or bug investigation.

argument_schema.name: scope-hint
argument_schema.description: Optional file, module, or subsystem path that bounds the evaluation.

loop: confirm task/worktree scope before cwd-resolving MCP reads
inspect the target area and classify findings by impact
tie each finding to a named smell or design pressure with evidence
sequence behavior-preserving refactorings into small testable steps
record findings and decisions through MCP when handoff durability matters

commands.makefile_target: (in-session bounded-loop skill; no standalone make target)
commands.description: Bounded autonomous bug-fix loop: commit a candidate fix per iteration, exit on the first passing test tied to HEAD, finalize with a slice-complete decision and a single post-loop close integrity check.
commands.execution_context: Use when iterating on a specific failing test inside an active feature-branch task. The loop uses bounded handoff reads per iteration, commits each candidate fix before testing so verified_tests provenance matches HEAD, and reserves integrity_check(payload={"kind":"close","enforce":true,"require_fresh_tests":true}) as the single post-loop pre-merge gate. Refuses to run on main/master/None target_branch.

argument_schema.name: failing-test-cmd
argument_schema.description: Failing test command the loop should drive to passing (e.g. 'make test-handoff TEST=tests/test_foo.py').

argument_schema.name: max-iterations
argument_schema.description: Iteration cap before recording a blocker and exiting non-zero. Default 5.

argument_schema.name: scope-hint
argument_schema.description: File path, module, or keyword that bounds the candidate-fix search space for each iteration.

loop: confirm active task has a feature target_branch (abort on main/master/None with zero MCP writes)
record an auto_fix_open decision to anchor the investigation trail
per iteration: get_handoff_state(sections='identity'), read implicated files, propose smallest edit, commit the fix, run failing_test_cmd, record test_result
exit the loop on the first passed=true test_result tied to HEAD, or record a blocker and exit non-zero at max_iterations

finalize: record slice_complete decision, set_handoff_state(status='done', status_only=True), call integrity_check(payload={"kind":"close","enforce":true,"require_fresh_tests":true,"current_commit_sha":<HEAD>}) exactly once
on Claude Code, gate inter-iteration waits to <270s warm-cache or >=1200s idle; Codex and Copilot iterate inline

commands.description: Task branch start, review gate, close-check, merge, and teardown for accepted-plan tasks or explicitly authorized maintenance with no task_plan_path.
commands.execution_context: Use when moving a plan-backed task from a reviewed, accepted plan baseline, or explicitly authorized maintenance with no task_plan_path, through branch start, review readiness, close-check, merge, and teardown; branch isolation and all verification, review, and close gates apply to both.

argument_schema.name: task-ref
argument_schema.description: Active task reference being started or finished.

argument_schema.name: objective
argument_schema.description: Task objective to pass to task-start when opening the branch.

loop: for plan-backed tasks, establish the reviewed, accepted plan baseline with make plan-accept before task-start and pass PLAN=docs/plans/<NNNN>-*.md to task-start; explicitly authorized maintenance with no task_plan_path has no approved-plan prerequisite
create or enter the task branch/worktree
verify alignment with make context
advance slices through /wb-tdd and /wb-implement
clear review-ready blockers and pass handoff-close-check
finish with the invariant close sequence and task teardown

commands.description: Implementation branch review workflow for lane or committed feature-branch diffs.
commands.execution_context: Use for implementation branch diffs, pre-merge review passes, and code audit requests.

argument_schema.name: scope
argument_schema.description: Optional explicit diff scope such as main...HEAD when reviewing a committed feature branch.

loop: decide whether the review scope is a lane/local working tree or a committed feature-branch diff
use make review-run only when reviewing lane/local working-tree scope
load the latest slice packet or branch diff
when the review is packet-backed, print the handoff decision string (`decision`) and numeric row id (`decision_id`)
pre-triage existing findings
run the branch-review checklist
record findings, verdict decision, and branch review run
refresh DASHBOARD.txt after state-changing handoff writes
confirm whether the branch is actually merge-ready

commands.description: Session start, task switching, and task-view regeneration workflow.
commands.execution_context: Use when starting or resuming a session, switching active tasks, or keeping generated task views aligned after MCP writes.

argument_schema.name: task-ref
argument_schema.description: Optional target task to switch into during the session.

loop: confirm branch/worktree context
load the current task state with bounded reads
externalize decisions, blockers, findings, and evidence at discovery through MCP; if unavailable, emit a structured worker report for coordinator durable recording without claiming successful writes
regenerate DASHBOARD.txt after non-atomic writes; use CURRENT_TASK.json only on demand
switch tasks safely and archive only after done

commands.makefile_target: (in-session root-cause skill; no standalone make target)
commands.description: Evidence-driven root-cause investigation with falsifiable experiments and finding-scoped outcomes.
commands.execution_context: Use when a symptom is known but its cause is unproven. Reproduce and observe the actual boundary before editing; independent investigations may proceed concurrently when their inputs and side effects permit it. Nonreproduction is an unresolved evidence gap, not proof of a fix or a reason by itself for wontfix.

argument_schema.name: symptom
argument_schema.description: Observed failure, error output, or unexpected behavior, with any reproduction evidence already available.

argument_schema.name: scope-hint
argument_schema.description: Optional owned file, module, test command, task reference, or subsystem that bounds experiments and affected findings.

loop: establish task/worktree scope before cwd-resolving reads
inspect actual producers, symptoms, reproduction steps, history, and relevant prior findings before mocks or mechanism claims
open a decision/evidence trail with symptoms, baseline, scope, and explicit affected ids; record only confirmed defects as review findings
for each hypothesis, predict a refuting observation and run a controlled experiment; serialize only experiments that share mutable state or dependent inputs
after refutations, reassess assumptions and seek independent evidence; escalate when a concrete missing input, scope, or environment blocker prevents progress
after confirming the cause, implement the smallest bounded fix and verify the original failing sequence and relevant regression checks
resolve only the explicit finding ids supported by commit-backed evidence; keep nonreproduced symptoms unresolved or defer them with the gap recorded
record the outcome and refresh the operator view; if MCP is unavailable, return evidence for coordinator durable recording

commands.execution_context: Use when decomposing active task-plan work into bounded implementation slices instead of horizontal layer-by-layer waves.

argument_schema.name: task-ref
argument_schema.description: Active task reference for the slice.

argument_schema.name: test-cmd
argument_schema.description: Failing test command used to open the slice.

loop: choose one end-to-end behavior path
advance the plan item cursor with a clean prior slice
open the slice through the tdd gate
keep the diff bounded to that one path
close with make slice-commit

commands.description: Pre-review planning draft using the eight analysis passes (0148/0189 /wb-draft rail; replaces the interim /wb-analyze id).
commands.execution_context: Use for pre-review triage of a planning artifact before the formal planning-review pass. Registered as /wb-draft, not /wb-analyze.

argument_schema.name: doc
argument_schema.description: Planning document path to analyze.

loop: load the plan, constitution, and minimal adjacent anchors
run the eight analysis passes
record findings with review_mode="planning"
record a planning review_run for this triage pass (no reserved session prefix)
recommend revise-first or proceed-to-planning-review

commands.description: Formal planning review workflow for task plans, epics, ADRs, and similar artifacts.
commands.execution_context: Use for task plans, epics, ADRs, and other planning artifacts that need formal review before implementation.

argument_schema.name: doc
argument_schema.description: Planning document path to review.

loop: load the planning doc and minimum code/contract anchors
run the planning-review checklist
record findings and verdict in MCP
print stable handoff gap ids (`finding_id`) when reporting findings
record the planning review run
refresh DASHBOARD.txt after state-changing handoff writes
block approval until open planning findings are resolved
after pass with zero open findings, direct the operator to make plan-accept before task-start

commands.makefile_target: (in-session coordinator skill; no standalone make target)
commands.description: Coordinator skill that fans out branch review by completed slice packet (one reviewer per slice by default), merges findings under the coordinator task_ref via review_findings(operation="merge"), and retires merged source rows. Falls back to whole-branch diff when no slice packets exist.
commands.execution_context: Use when a branch review benefits from independent reviewers partitioned by slice (default) or, when no slice packets exist, parallel whole-branch reviewers. The coordinator stays inside its harness and routes fan-out through the cheapest in-process subagent primitive.

argument_schema.name: reviewers-per-slice
argument_schema.description: Reviewers to fan out per completed slice. Default 1. Legacy reviewers-count aliases here when slice mode is active.

argument_schema.name: reviewers-count
argument_schema.description: Legacy alias for reviewers-per-slice in slice mode; whole-branch fallback still uses this as reviewer count (default 2).

argument_schema.name: reviewer-prompt-template
argument_schema.description: Optional prompt template id resolved under config/agent-workflows/prompts/wb-review-slice/ (harness-neutral).

loop: confirm coordinator has an active task_ref and feature branch
enumerate completed slices via search_handoff(slice_complete) and fetch each packet via get_latest_slice_review_packet(slice_decision_id=...); whole-branch fallback when zero slices
pick a round token and assign each reviewer a scoped task_ref using <task>-REV-<round>-S<n>-<letter> (fallback: <task>-REV-<round>-<letter>)
invoke reviewers via the harness routing table with per-slice git diff <commit>~1..<commit> restricted to packet changed_files
each reviewer records findings under its scoped task_ref via review_findings(operation='batch_record')
coordinator merges per slice with review_findings(operation='merge', retire_sources=true) under the coordinator task_ref
run one harmonization reviewer (<task>-REV-<round>-HARM-A) on integration lenses only, then merge under the coordinator
coordinator records exactly one branch-mode review_runs entry for the combined pass

commands.description: Real-behavior RED to GREEN verification inside a bounded implementation slice.
commands.execution_context: Use before production edits for a behavior change. RED must exercise the actual behavior with representative real inputs and fail for the intended reason. Gate only implementation that consumes that evidence; unrelated slices may proceed independently. Documentation protocol corrections use existing materialization/contracts rather than fabricated failing tests.

argument_schema.name: task-ref
argument_schema.description: Active task reference for the bounded behavior slice.

argument_schema.name: test-cmd
argument_schema.description: Command demonstrating the intended behavioral RED on representative real inputs before implementation, then GREEN after the change.

loop: define the observable behavior, real inputs, expected result, and falsifiable failure prediction
inspect the actual producer before introducing mocks; retain optional-dependency failure behavior
run a relevant existing or new behavior check and confirm intended RED rather than syntax, import, environment, or blanket assertion noise
record real RED evidence with make slice-start before the dependent production edit; do not require a separate dispatch when one lane can perform both steps
implement the smallest bounded change and re-run the same check to GREEN
refactor while GREEN; after any commit rewrite refresh verification against the final HEAD, then hand off to make slice-commit

commands.makefile_target: (in-session cross-harness offload skill; no standalone make target)
commands.description: Bounded offload with an explicit agent, receipt-resolved routing, idempotent dispatch, typed outcomes, and coordinator review.
commands.execution_context: Use for a self-contained lane with explicit inputs, owned paths, and a structured end-state contract. Supported backend/model/effort choices and timeout bounds come from the live registry, capability/preflight receipt, and AgentSpec, not prose inventories. Require an explicit agent; refuse unavailable capabilities or dependencies with their typed failure and never silently substitute a backend.

argument_schema.name: objective
argument_schema.description: Self-contained lane objective with explicit inputs, owned paths, acceptance criteria, and a structured output contract.

argument_schema.name: agent
argument_schema.description: Explicit offload backend: grok-remote, grok-cli, cursor-cli, cursor-remote, codex-remote, codex-subagent, or openrouter-remote (normalized via validate_backend; no fallback, no implicit default). `grok-remote` is discontinued by the operator; never a default for dispatch. Under a remote_only ledger every REMOTE_OFFLOAD_BACKENDS member (codex-remote, cursor-remote, grok-remote, openrouter-remote) stays explicitly selectable, and an explicit local backend is refused with the typed remote_required outcome. Admission additionally requires live-registry validation and capability/preflight evidence.

argument_schema.name: effort
argument_schema.description: Required requested reasoning effort supported by the selected backend; use registry capability/preflight evidence for valid choices and preserve the resolved AgentSpec value.

argument_schema.name: token-budget
argument_schema.description: Required caller-owned per-lane token budget, checked by preflight and preserved across continuation cycles.

argument_schema.name: lane-id
argument_schema.description: Optional lane identity for its worktree and isolated resources; default derived from the explicit agent.

argument_schema.name: task-ref
argument_schema.description: Optional active task reference; defaults to the current handoff task after scope verification.

loop: confirm active feature-branch task and a bounded lane contract with inputs, owned paths, scoped TEST_CMD, known-red evidence, and structured output
require an explicit agent and requested effort; use list_available_backends and capability evidence for supported backend/model/effort choices without an implicit default
run offload_preflight with requested routing, budget, and worktree; preserve optional-dependency refusals and use receipt-resolved model, effort, execution mode, and timeout bounds
manage_worktree_lane upsert and materialize_offload_lane_manifest with explicit backend and requested routing policy; preserve receipt/AgentSpec effective values without recomputing defaults
dispatch_lane_work with the bounded brief, dispatch_id idempotency key, admitted routing, and start_worker=false
run_offload_pass with caller-owned token_budget and receipt-supported timeout_seconds/turn_timeout_seconds; native remote execution uses the existing scripts/remote_agent.sh AgentSpec transport
branch only on the typed outcome; on still_running or client disconnect use bounded await_offload_pass continuation without polling or background monitors

present the committed diff, scoped verification, and remaining gaps for coordinator branch-complete /wb-review-slice over all landed product commits; /wb-review-code remains optional in-lane smoke; no fallback or automatic merge

delegate to `workbay embeddings --status|--enable|--disable` (cwd=workspace root; bootstrap alias is deprecated)
summarize enabled/disabled state and source for the operator

commands.description: Text-first UX map: author/render/critique .uxmap.json inventory and optional FREEFORM flow projection.
commands.execution_context: Use when decomposing SPA/Workbench UI work from screens/zones/states/flows, editing .uxmap.json, or running heuristic critique before UI slices.

load or upsert .uxmap.json; author jobs→screens→zones→states→actions→flows

run critique; fix high/medium before UI slice-start; optional emit to handoff when task_ref set

hooks.description: Managed stop-hook adapter declarations for compact-session wiring.
Managed SessionStart adapter declarations for handoff.db context re-injection (internal / implementation note).
hooks.rationale: Re-injection relies on SessionStart stdout being added to model context, which only Claude Code provides today; the internal generated session_start family for codex/vscode is always-on (no install-time opt-in) and its injection semantic is unverified there. Revisit when an opt-in surface or verified injection semantic exists.

hooks.description: Fresh-clone self-heal: regenerate gitignored agent surfaces (plugins-build + generate-agent-workflows) when missing.
hooks.rationale: Script body ships once under scripts/hooks/ (shared, already fenced). Claude base always-on registration is harness-protocol session_start / settings.hooks.json (wholesale write) — NO claude-code adapter here, which would double-register against that base. Non-claude adapters mirror compact-session multi-harness shape and are opt-in only so a harness with no selected adapter registers nothing (no crash).
